is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae species complex (An. gambiae, An. coluzzii, and Goundry form).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports genotyping of the Vgsc L995F (L1014F) marker.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The paper provides sample sizes for the Goundry group (n=264) and reports genotype-based association results (e.g., n=84 homozygous for HapA, n=180 for other haplotypes) in Figure 2B and the text on page 6.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected as larvae in the village of Goundry, Burkina Faso (page 2).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study involving field collection, SNP genotyping, and functional RNAi assays.

sub_country_location.evidence: Collections were done in the village of Goundry (12°30′N, 1°20′W), Burkina Faso (page 2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collections were done across months of the malaria transmission season of 2007 and 2008 (page 2).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes new collections and experimental infections performed by the authors.

supplement.evidence: The necessary genotype data and sample sizes are provided in the main text and figures.

assessment.summary: This study investigates the genetic association between the para-bearing haplotype (containing the kdr L1014F mutation) and Plasmodium falciparum susceptibility in wild Anopheles mosquitoes from Burkina Faso. Using SNP genotyping and functional RNAi-mediated gene silencing, the authors demonstrate that while the kdr-bearing haplotype is associated with increased susceptibility, the para gene itself does not directly influence parasite infection levels, whereas the immune gene ClipC9 does.
